title: Folded cascode OTA
description: A folded cascode: the input pair steers current into a folding node, and a cascoded output branch carries it to a high-impedance output. It is the branch-current bookkeeping showcase. The tail is drawn the way the circuit sets it: only the bias reference is programmed, with $I_{tail}$; the tail device shares its gate and width and delivers the programmed current less the mirror's drain-voltage error, and the input pair carries half of what it delivers. Each folding-branch current source is biased at $I_{branch}$, and the output cascode and mirror carry the fold current $I_{fold}$, the branch bias less the input device's current — a later child reads the earlier input device's provided current to compute its own bias. The fold current is a real design knob: it must be at least the input device's current, so that when slewing steers the whole tail current into one folding node the branch there never starves, but the folding current sources add input-referred noise, so more fold current trades noise for slew headroom. Gain is $g_{m,in}$ times the folded-cascode output resistance; unlike the telescopic it separates the input CM range from the output swing, at the cost of the extra branch current and its noise. The stack is parameterized by its NODES: the tail node is pinned so the produced $CM_{in}$ equals $CM_{dc}$, and the folding node $V_{fold}$ and the mirror-drain node $V_c$ are choice params — every device $V_{DS}$ is a subtraction between adjacent nodes and every source-above-bulk device carries its true body bias, so the drops close each branch by construction. The retired per-device estimates could not even agree on where the folding node sat; the node form makes that inconsistency inexpressible.

params.name: vn_target
params.note: input-referred thermal density budget. The folding current sources are the fold's noise price: with each device's noise read from the tables, the row lands near 42.4 nV/rtHz on a sky130 tt realization with the PMOS devices on the pfet table, over this budget and well above a telescopic at the same gm. No simulated floor exists for this topology

params.name: vos_target
params.note: input offset budget, 1 sigma; the output mirror's spread referred through the fold puts the total near 5.9 mV on a sky130 tt realization, with the pair, the folding sources and the mirror all at 1 um

params.name: CM_lo
params.note: input CM range the application presents, low edge — checked exactly by the cm-lo edge at every evaluation (the sweep put the widest closing range at 0.92-1.64 V on sky130 tt at the shipped choices: below it the tail device leaves saturation, and above it the tail node runs out of its search range). The edge checks the ENDPOINT; the interior is the sweep's to show

params.name: CM_hi
params.note: input CM range the application presents, high edge — its ENDPOINT checked by the cm-hi edge the same way

params.name: CM_dc
params.note: the input common mode the application presents. The engine places the tail node so the sheet sits exactly here; sweep it to trace the common-mode axis

params.name: V_out_dc
params.note: output DC level; the NMOS-side nodes climb to it and the folding node descends to it. The PMOS and NMOS cascodes meet at a high-impedance output that nothing on this sheet holds; the feedback the application closes around the amplifier holds it here

params.name: V_tail
params.note: the tail node — the pair's source. Solved rather than set: searched between min and max (the range it is searched in, not slider bounds) until the produced common mode equals CM_dc

params.name: V_fold
params.note: the folding node: input-pair drains, folding-source drain, and PMOS-cascode source in one. The input vds is V_fold - V_tail, the folding source's is VDD - V_fold, and the PMOS cascode's is V_fold - V_out_dc — by construction. Stated at this design point. Where the design is held fixed (a range end), the gate bias above this node is what stays put and the node is re-solved under it, between min and max.

params.name: V_c
params.note: the NMOS-side internal node: mirror drain and NMOS-cascode source. The mirror vds is V_c and the cascode's is V_out_dc - V_c, by construction. Stated at this design point. Where the design is held fixed (a range end), the gate bias above this node is what stays put and the node is re-solved under it, between min and max.

params.name: avt
params.note: Pelgrom A_VT

params.name: abeta
params.note: Pelgrom A_beta

params.name: sign_p
params.note: vds sign convention of the PMOS-side tables: +1 for an N-style axis, -1 for a signed-PMOS axis

params.name: I_tail
params.note: the current the bias reference is programmed to — the one tail current on this sheet that is typed. The tail device mirrors it 1:1 through the shared gate and delivers it less the mirror's drain-voltage error (the tail node sits below the reference's diode drop); the input pair's transconductance and the slew rate are computed from what is delivered, not from this number

params.name: I_branch
params.note: folding-branch bias current; the fold current I_fold, this less the input device's current, must stay at least that current (slew headroom vs current-source noise)

params.name: gm_id_in
params.note: input-pair inversion: sets gm per current and the input-referred noise

params.name: gm_id_casc
params.note: cascode-device inversion: higher gm/ID lifts cascode gain but costs vdsat headroom

params.name: gm_id_cs
params.note: current-source and mirror inversion: lower gm/ID adds less noise and offset

params.name: L_in
params.note: length of the input pair: at 1 um its area takes the pair's share of the offset under budget with the pair carrying half of what the tail delivers

params.name: L_cs
params.note: length of the folding current sources and of the output mirror. Their output resistance sets the gain and the mirror's area the larger part of the offset, so they are long — 1 um, with the input pair at the same length: at half a micron, pair and current sources both, the design misses its offset budget at the low end of its common-mode range on a sky130 tt realization

params.name: gm_id_tail
params.note: inversion level of the bias reference, which the tail device inherits through the shared gate: a higher V* costs headroom at the tail node

params.name: L_tail
params.note: length of the bias reference and of the tail device, which mirror at one length: longer shrinks the mirror's drain-voltage error

doc.title: Tail bias reference
doc.description: The diode-connected reference the programmed current $I_{tail}$ flows into — the one device on this sheet whose current is typed. Its drain is its gate, so its $V_{DS}$ is its own $V_{GS}$ and the table is read along that diagonal with nothing estimated. It publishes its width and its gate voltage, which is all the tail device needs to copy it.

doc.title: Tail current source
doc.description: The tail device, on the bias reference's gate at the reference's width: a 1:1 mirror of the programmed current, with $V_{tail}$ as its drain-source voltage. Its current is read off the table rather than typed — the reference sits at its own diode drop and this device at $V_{tail}$, so it delivers the programmed current scaled by what that difference in $V_{DS}$ does through its $g_{ds}$. It has to stay saturated, and it leaves saturation when $V_{tail}$ falls below its own $V_{dsat}$, which is what sets the low end of the usable common-mode range.

params.name: W_t
params.note: the bias reference's width — a 1:1 copy

params.name: vgs_t
params.note: the bias reference's gate voltage — the gate wire the two share

params.name: vds_t
params.note: the tail node

doc.title: Input-pair device
doc.description: Half-circuit input device, carrying half of what the tail delivers; it evaluates before the folding branch so the branch can read its current.

doc.title: Folding current source (PMOS)
doc.description: The top current source biased at I_branch; feeds the folding node. Its ro (cascoded) sets the PMOS-side output resistance, and it adds input-referred noise.

doc.title: PMOS cascode (folded branch)
doc.description: Cascodes the folding current source; carries the fold current I_fold, the branch bias less the current read from the input device. Its av0 sets the PMOS-side cascode boost.

doc.title: NMOS cascode (output branch)
doc.description: Cascodes the NMOS mirror; carries the fold current. Its av0 sets the NMOS-side cascode boost.

doc.title: NMOS mirror (output branch)
doc.description: Bottom of the output branch; its ro (cascoded by ncasc) sets the NMOS-side output resistance, and it adds input-referred noise.

equations.name: CM_in
equations.note: the input common mode this bias produces — an OUTPUT here, not a setting; rises monotonically with the tail node, so the pin is a well-posed one-unknown search

equations.name: tail_headroom
equations.note: how far the tail node sits above the tail device's saturation edge — exact, because the tail node is the variable rather than something inferred from a common mode

equations.name: I_fold
equations.note: the folded branch current: the branch bias minus the peak steered input current

equations.name: Rout_p
equations.note: PMOS side: the folding current source ro boosted by the PMOS-cascode gain

equations.name: Rout_n
equations.note: NMOS side: the output mirror ro boosted by the NMOS-cascode gain

equations.name: Rout
equations.note: the two cascoded sides in parallel. The gain assumes a capacitive load, so nothing here models a resistive one; this row is what a composing parent checks its own loading against

equations.name: SR
equations.note: the whole tail current steered into the load — the current the tail device delivers, not the number the reference is programmed to

equations.name: vn_in
equations.note: input pair plus the top and bottom current-source pairs, each at its own density; the folding sources are the price of the fold

equations.name: vos
equations.expr: sqrt(pelgrom_vos(avt, abeta, in__W, L_in, gm_id_in)^2 + (pelgrom_vos(avt, abeta, nmir__W, L_cs, gm_id_cs)*nmir__gm/in__gm)^2)
equations.note: input-pair offset plus the output-mirror offset referred by the gm ratio

equations.name: cgg_in
equations.note: estimate: the capacitance one input terminal presents — the gate capacitance of a single input device. Gate capacitance only, because the Miller term needs the gate-drain fraction and these tables do not carry it, so a driving stage sees more than this. No rule reads it

equations.name: I_q
equations.note: estimate: quiescent supply current — both folding current sources, which are the only devices sitting on the supply rail. The tail current is not a third branch: it is drawn down THROUGH those sources and returned to ground by the tail device, so 2*I_branch already contains it and equals the other way of writing the same number, what the tail delivers plus 2*I_fold. The reference branch that programs the tail is shared bias infrastructure and is not counted here. The datasheet line for comparing designs; no rule reads it

checks.note: the folded branch must carry at least what the input device does, so that when slewing steers the whole tail current into one folding node the branch there does not starve

reads each device's thermal noise from the table where the table carries it, and the gamma = 1 estimate where it does not; it stays advisory because a sheet cannot know which table it will be evaluated on, and the simulator owns noise sign-off
the common mode this bias produces has to sit inside the range the application presents
paired with cm-not-below; the cm-lo/cm-hi edges check that the design covers the range ENDS, and the CM_dc sweep shows the whole landscape

operatingRange.name: cm-lo
operatingRange.note: the claimed low edge, checked exactly: the whole sheet re-evaluates at CM_dc = CM_lo on the design this run produced — its own tail-node solve over its full range, every device held at the geometry it was sized to — and every hard rule must hold there

operatingRange.name: cm-hi
operatingRange.note: the claimed high edge, checked the same way. The edges check the ENDPOINTS; the CM_dc sweep remains the authority on the full landscape
